subject: ventures/workflow-audit
professional: a senior application-security engineer who reviews GitHub Actions CI/CD supply chains (the kind of reviewer who runs zizmor and reads GitHub Security Lab advisories); they check first whether the high-severity classes (pwn-request checkout, script injection including actions/github-script, workflow_run artifact execution, cache poisoning) are actually reported on known-vulnerable fixtures, then false positives on the documented safe pattern (intermediate env var), then SHA pinning, then whether the SARIF lands correctly in Code Scanning

evidence.correctness: Ran a 19-case fixture battery (python3 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/4d40ef56-18b0-5820-a3ae-5a4c926539dc/scratchpad/workflow-audit/run.py /home/user/oss-monorepo/ventures/workflow-audit/audit.py) with expected outcomes typed from GitHub's hardening docs and Security Lab posts: 14/19 pass. Right: github.head_ref and issue.title injection in single-line and multi-line run blocks, head_commit.message, the env-intermediate mitigation not flagged, github.sha not flagged, pwn-request via pull_request.head.ref, short SHA flagged and full SHA accepted, write-all, missing permissions, missing timeout, timeout 360 (GitHub default) flagged, fork-reachable self-hosted runner, secrets: inherit on pull_request_target, base64 of a secret. Wrong: (1) the merge layer silently drops three risk classes its own vendored checkers report (python3 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/4d40ef56-18b0-5820-a3ae-5a4c926539dc/scratchpad/workflow-audit/dropped.py /home/user/oss-monorepo/ventures/workflow-audit): artifact-executed-after-untrusted-download (audit.py:43 maps the misspelt key 'artifact-executed', so the page's headline High item never appears; a workflow_run job that downloads a PR artifact and runs bash ./build.sh gets only a medium 'unscoped-artifact-download'), checkout-persists-credentials-with-upload (the ArtiPACKED shape, the worse of the two checkout cases, is reported as nothing while the milder shape is reported), and shut-down-version (actions/upload-artifact@v3, which no longer runs). (2) Not detected: injection in actions/github-script `script:` (GitHub's own example), workflow_run.head_branch, checkout of refs/pull/N/merge under pull_request_target, toJSON(secrets). The per-check logic is mostly right; the product's own layer is wrong on a high-severity class, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features exercised: composite Action inputs (path, fail-on, sarif-file, baseline) read from action.yml, CLI text/json/markdown/sarif (tests run all four), fail-on thresholds, baseline with line-shift tolerance and duplicate counting, inline ignore with rule list, error on missing baseline, deploy-concurrency adapter, drift guard against 11 source ventures (all 11 byte-identical, checked with cmp). Not working end to end: three of the advertised risk classes (artifacts executed on untrusted triggers, credentials persisted with upload, end-of-life action versions that no longer run) never reach the report. The Action itself was not run on a GitHub runner from this session.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/workflow-audit && python3 -m unittest test_audit: 16 tests OK in 7.5 s; node --test page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs: 14 pass. Five mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (baseline budget > to >=; fail-on >= to >), 3 survived: severity of unmasked-env-export medium to low, inline-ignore also honouring the line below, and renaming the cache-poisoning rule key so it no longer matches (the exact bug class that already shipped for artifact-executed). No test asserts that every RISK_CLASSIFICATIONS entry of a vendored checker is mapped in CHECKS, and only 3 of 27 rule names are asserted end to end.
evidence.craft: Read audit.py (356 lines), action.yml, test_audit.py, checks/injection.py, checks/artifact-poisoning.py, checks/checkout-credentials.py, checks/runtime-deprecation.py, checks/unpinned-action.py headers. audit.py is small, readable, subprocess-isolated, errors surfaced as warnings. Defects: rule names are hand-typed strings in CHECKS rather than read from each checker's RISK_CLASSIFICATIONS, and an unknown rule is dropped silently as 'informational' with no warning (audit.py:119-122), which is how three risk classes vanished; SARIF helpUri points to https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/workflow-audit/ which returns 404 (audit.py:290), so every Code Scanning alert links to a dead page; the Action scans the tree four times (action.yml run block) instead of once and rendering four formats; no partialFingerprints in SARIF.
evidence.claims: Backed: disclaimer, no warranty, no SLA, 'not a security audit', no network calls (no urllib/socket/http in audit.py or checks; page.test.mjs), MIT, zizmor named honestly as broader. Served page https://marisstella.app/workflow-audit/ loaded (200, 21 KB) and matches source apart from build chrome. Unbacked: page 'What it checks' table lists 'artifacts executed ... on untrusted triggers' as High and 'actions on end-of-life runtimes' as Low; neither the executed-artifact rule nor shut-down-version is ever reported. README:65 'Informational classifications are dropped' is false: risk classifications are dropped too. README:50 'On this monorepo the scan finds 1,182' is stale: the scan today finds 13 (0 high, 10 medium, 3 low) over 129 workflows. llms.txt carries the calculator boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', which does not describe a workflow scanner.
evidence.fitness: Walked a maintainer's job: add the documented four-line step, get a job summary, fail on high. The flow works on the CLI on fixtures and on this monorepo (0.6 s). Gaps a maintainer hits: the recommended ref Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo/ventures/workflow-audit@main makes the runner download the whole monorepo tree (git ls-tree: about 1,074 MB tracked) on every job that uses it; a workflow_run artifact-execution pwn, the most common high-impact pattern in recent advisories, comes back with no high finding, so fail-on: high passes; github-script injections pass silently. The README is honest that zizmor is deeper.
evidence.domain: Compared against GitHub Docs, 'Security hardening for GitHub Actions' (untrusted-input list, actions/github-script example, intermediate env-var mitigation, pin to full-length commit SHA) and GitHub Security Lab 'Keeping your GitHub Actions and workflows secure' parts 1-4 (pwn requests, untrusted input, workflow_run artifacts); expected outcomes typed into the fixture before running, from those sources, not from the checkers' own docstrings, and zizmor's audit set (template-injection incl. github-script, artipacked, dangerous-triggers, unpinned-uses, cache-poisoning, excessive-permissions). Matches practice: the env-var mitigation, full-SHA pinning (short SHA rejected), first-party vs third-party owner split, timeout default 360, fork-exposed self-hosted runners as high, secrets: inherit. Departs: injection only in run: (not github-script script:, the docs' own example), workflow_run.head_branch not treated as untrusted, the refs/pull/N/merge pwn-request variant missed, toJSON(secrets) not flagged, and the merge layer drops artipacked and workflow_run artifact execution.

verdict: A tidy, honest-in-tone aggregator whose eleven vendored checkers are byte-identical to their source ventures and mostly right on fixtures typed from GitHub's hardening docs (14 of 19 plus 3 of 3). The product's own layer, a hand-typed rule-to-severity map, silently drops three risk classes its checkers report: workflow_run artifact execution (advertised as High), the ArtiPACKED checkout-with-upload shape, and action versions that no longer run. A maintainer who adds fail-on: high would pass a workflow_run artifact pwn. Tests pass but 3 of 5 seeded mutations survive, including a rule-key rename, the bug class that shipped. Coverage also misses github-script injection and the merge-ref pwn request. Below the bar on correctness, claims and verification; not finished.
